moods.name: Calm
moods.tagline: For when everything feels too loud.
moods.description: A short piece written to slow you down — no breathing app, no advice, just two minutes where nothing is being asked of you.
moods.whatThisIs: Seven short paragraphs that move at the speed you wish today had. It doesn't tell you to relax. It just stops asking.
moods.teaserTitle: Nothing is asking anything of you right now
moods.teaser: Let your eyes rest on this, not read it exactly, just move across it slowly. Breathe in for four. Hold for four. Out for six. You don't need to count out loud — just let the rhythm happen underneath everything else you're thinking about.
moods.teaserTail: Your shoulders have been climbing toward your ears for longer than you realized. Let them drop.
moods.shareLine: Nothing is asking anything of you right now.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when everything feels too loud
moods.seoKeywords: something calming to read, short writing to slow down, two minute read to calm down

moods.name: Nostalgia
moods.tagline: For when you miss a version of your life that doesn't exist anymore.
moods.description: A short piece about the light in a room you can't go back to, and the person you were standing in it.
moods.whatThisIs: A walk back through the small, specific details memory keeps — the ones that aren't about a place at all.
moods.teaser: The particular gold of late afternoon light through a car window on a drive home from somewhere ordinary. The specific quiet of a house on a Sunday morning before anyone else was awake. A voice calling your name from another room, the exact pitch of it, gone now, but not really —
moods.teaserTail: still filed somewhere in you, ready to surface. There's a version of you that existed in that light.
moods.shareLine: You don't miss the place. You miss who you were there.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you miss how things used to be
moods.seoKeywords: nostalgic writing, something to read when you miss the past, short nostalgic story

moods.name: Happiness
moods.tagline: For when you forgot you're allowed to feel good.
moods.description: A short piece that hands back the lightness you've been treating as something you have to earn.
moods.whatThisIs: Two minutes of permission. Not a pep talk — nobody here is going to tell you to be grateful.
moods.teaserTitle: The lightness you forgot you had
moods.teaser: Notice this: right now, nothing is required of you. Not one thing. Let your shoulders find out how far down they can actually go. You are allowed to feel good for no reason — you don't need a permission slip, an achievement, a reason the size of your worry.
moods.teaserTail: Happiness doesn't have to be earned back like a debt. Sometimes it just arrives.
moods.shareLine: Happiness doesn't have to be earned back like a debt.
moods.seoTitle: Something short to read when you want to feel lighter
moods.seoKeywords: short uplifting writing, something to read to feel better, short inspirational writing

moods.name: Hope
moods.description: A short piece for the part of the night that hasn't broken yet, written without a single promise it can't keep.
moods.whatThisIs: About how change starts before there's any proof of it. No timeline, no guarantee, no forced optimism.
moods.teaserTitle: It's still dark, and the sky is already changing
moods.teaser: You can't see it yet, not really — the light hasn't reached the part of the sky you're looking at. But somewhere past the horizon, it's already begun. That's how mornings work. The change starts before there's any proof of it.
moods.teaserTail: You've been asking things to be different for a while now, and nothing you can point to has shifted.
moods.shareLine: The change starts before there's any proof of it.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when tomorrow feels uncertain
moods.seoKeywords: something hopeful to read, short writing about hope, words for a hard week

moods.name: Hurt
moods.description: A short piece about what someone's choice revealed, and why that's the part that keeps stinging.
moods.whatThisIs: It doesn't take their side and it doesn't tell you to let it go. It just names the thing accurately.
moods.teaserTitle: You have every right to feel this
moods.teaser: Someone you trusted did something that trust wasn't built for. Maybe they said it plainly. Maybe they just showed you, through what they chose over you, exactly how much room you took up in their decisions. Not much, it turns out. Not enough.
moods.teaserTail: That's the part that stings worst — not the moment itself, but what it revealed.
moods.shareLine: Not the moment itself. What it revealed.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when someone hurt you
moods.seoKeywords: short writing about being hurt, something to read after being let down, short stories about heartbreak

moods.name: Sorrow
moods.tagline: For the days that feel heavier than usual.
moods.description: A letter that sits down next to you instead of trying to move you along.
moods.whatThisIs: Written as a letter. It does not say it gets better, because you've heard that and it didn't help.
moods.teaser: I'm not going to tell you it gets better. Not yet. Right now I just want to sit here with you, in the part where it's heavy, and not rush you toward the door marked “fine.”
moods.teaserTail: Some things don't resolve. They just get carried differently over time.
moods.shareLine: Some things don't resolve. They just get carried differently.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you're sad and don't want advice
moods.seoKeywords: things to read when you're sad, short sad writing, something to read on a heavy day

moods.name: Grief
moods.tagline: For someone or something you still carry with you.
moods.description: A letter written to the shape a person left behind, and to the habits that haven't caught up yet.
moods.whatThisIs: For the ordinary ambushes — a stranger's laugh, a coat like theirs. It calls that love, not failure to move on.
moods.teaserTitle: To the shape they left behind,
moods.teaser: I know you still set the table for one more sometimes, out of habit, before you remember. I know their voice still catches you off guard in ordinary places — a stranger's laugh, a song on the radio, a coat like the one they used to wear.
moods.teaserTail: That's not you being unable to move on. That's just what love does when it loses its address.
moods.shareLine: That's just what love does when it loses its address.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you're grieving someone
moods.seoKeywords: something to read when grieving, short writing about grief, words for someone you lost

moods.name: Rage
moods.tagline: For the feeling you don't know where to put.
moods.description: A short piece that agrees with you. No breathing exercise, no both-sides, no calming down.
moods.whatThisIs: Permission to be furious at the correct size. It is the loudest thing on the shelf and it is not sorry.
moods.teaser: You've been so reasonable for so long. Explaining calmly. Giving the benefit of the doubt one more time than it was owed. Swallowing the sharp thing you wanted to say because it wasn't “the right moment.” There's never a right moment for people like that.
moods.teaserTail: You are not too much for being furious about this. You are correctly sized.
moods.shareLine: You are not too much for being furious about this. You are correctly sized.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you're angry and tired of being reasonable
moods.seoKeywords: something to read when you're angry, short writing about anger, where to put anger

moods.name: Love
moods.tagline: For when someone occupies your thoughts.
moods.description: A piece about the quiet, constant kind of love — the sort that arrives in the gaps of an ordinary day.
moods.whatThisIs: For the stage before anything is settled, when someone has simply moved into your attention and won't leave.
moods.teaserTitle: They keep arriving in the middle of things
moods.teaser: You were doing something ordinary. Filling a glass, locking a door, halfway through a sentence to somebody else. And there they were again, arriving the way weather does. It isn't dramatic. Nobody warns you about that part — that love mostly happens in the gaps. In the three seconds before the kettle boils. In the walk from the car to the front door.
moods.teaserTail: You've started noticing things on their behalf. A song they'd like.
moods.shareLine: Love mostly happens in the gaps.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you can't stop thinking about someone
moods.seoKeywords: something to read when you like someone, short writing about love, words for thinking about someone
body: You were doing something ordinary. Filling a glass, locking a door, halfway through a sentence to somebody else. And there they were again, arriving the way weather does.
It isn't dramatic. Nobody warns you about that part — that love mostly happens in the gaps. In the three seconds before the kettle boils. In the walk from the car to the front door.
You've started noticing things on their behalf. A song they'd like. A particular blue. The way the light does something at six o'clock that you'd want them to see.
That's what it is, mostly. Not the declarations. The running commentary you've started keeping for an audience of one.
You don't know yet what any of it comes to. Whether it's returned in the same shape. Whether it lasts the winter. Whether you ever say it out loud.
But something in you has already decided to carry them around, and it didn't ask you first.
Let it be unresolved tonight. You're allowed to simply be full of someone.

moods.name: Heartbreak
moods.tagline: For the nights when you still think about them.
moods.description: A piece about the conversation that never happens, and the future you lost along with the person.
moods.whatThisIs: For the rehearsing stage — when your mind keeps staging the talk that would fix it, and the ending holds anyway.
moods.teaserTitle: It isn't the missing. It's the rehearsing.
moods.teaser: You've had the conversation again tonight — the one that never happens. You said the right thing this time. They understood. It still didn't help. That's the part that exhausts you. Not the missing exactly, but the rehearsing. Your mind keeps staging it, looking for the version where it ends differently.
moods.teaserTail: There isn't one. You've checked every angle by now, at every hour, and the ending holds.
moods.shareLine: You're not being pathetic. You're being someone who meant it.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you're still thinking about them
moods.seoKeywords: something to read after a breakup, short writing about heartbreak, words for missing an ex
body: You've had the conversation again tonight — the one that never happens. You said the right thing this time. They understood. It still didn't help.
That's the part that exhausts you. Not the missing exactly, but the rehearsing. Your mind keeps staging it, looking for the version where it ends differently.
There isn't one. You've checked every angle by now, at every hour, and the ending holds.
Somewhere in the last few weeks you stopped missing the person and started missing the future — the one with them in it, already furnished, that you had quietly been living in.
That future was real to you. Losing it is a real loss, even though nobody sends flowers for it.
You will stop rehearsing. Not tonight, and not because you decided to. One ordinary evening you'll notice the conversation didn't run, and you'll already be somewhere else.
Until then: you're not being pathetic. You're being someone who meant it.

moods.name: Restless
moods.tagline: For thoughts that only arrive when everyone else is asleep.
moods.description: A piece for the hour when the house is quiet and your mind decides to audit you.
moods.whatThisIs: For 2am — when knowing a thought isn't true does nothing at all to stop it.
moods.teaserTitle: The hours that don't belong to anyone
moods.teaser: It's late in the way that stops being late and starts being early. The house has gone quiet in that particular way, and your thoughts have got louder to fill it. Almost nothing you think at this hour survives the morning. You know that. It doesn't help, because at 2am knowing something is not the same as believing it.
moods.teaserTail: This is when the mind audits you. Old conversations.
moods.shareLine: At 2am, knowing something is not the same as believing it.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you can't sleep at 2am
moods.seoKeywords: something to read at 2am, short writing for insomnia, words for racing thoughts at night
body: It's late in the way that stops being late and starts being early. The house has gone quiet in that particular way, and your thoughts have got louder to fill it.
Almost nothing you think at this hour survives the morning. You know that. It doesn't help, because at 2am knowing something is not the same as believing it.
This is when the mind audits you. Old conversations. Something you said at nineteen. A decision from three years ago it has chosen to reopen tonight, without warning.
None of it is urgent. All of it feels urgent. That's the trick of this hour — it hands you real things at the one time you can do nothing about any of them.
You are not failing at sleep. You are awake in a quiet house, which people have been doing for as long as there have been houses.
Nothing is being decided right now. The audit closes on its own.
Put it down. It will still be there at a reasonable hour, and so will you.

moods.name: Longing
moods.tagline: For someone you can't quite let go of.
moods.description: A piece about the message you keep almost sending, and why missing someone isn't a problem to solve.
moods.whatThisIs: For the reaching-for-your-phone moment, and the part of you that feels embarrassed about it.
moods.teaser: The message is written. It has been for a while now — in your head if not in your phone — and you keep almost sending it. You've found reasons not to. Good ones, mostly. It's late. It's been too long. It would reopen something you have nearly finished closing.
moods.teaserTail: But the wanting doesn't take instruction. It arrives when a song does, or when something happens that only they would have found funny, and you reach for your phone before you remember you'd stopped doing that.
moods.shareLine: You can hold someone in mind without holding them in your life.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you miss someone you shouldn't text
moods.seoKeywords: something to read when you miss someone, short writing about longing, words for wanting to text them
body: The message is written. It has been for a while now — in your head if not in your phone — and you keep almost sending it.
You've found reasons not to. Good ones, mostly. It's late. It's been too long. It would reopen something you have nearly finished closing.

But the wanting doesn't take instruction. It arrives when a song does, or when something happens that only they would have found funny, and you reach for your phone before you remember you'd stopped doing that.
Missing someone isn't a problem to be solved. It's evidence — of a real thing, that was real, and hasn't finished being real in you yet.
Nobody gets to time that for you. Not them, not the people who think you should be over it, and not the version of you reading this and feeling faintly embarrassed.
You can hold someone in mind without holding them in your life. Those are different rooms.
Put the phone down tonight. You can miss them in the morning too.

moods.name: Mending
moods.tagline: For when you're slowly becoming okay again.
moods.description: A piece for the week you noticed you were fine, and didn't quite trust it.
moods.whatThisIs: For the suspicious part of recovery — treating a good week as weather rather than climate.
moods.teaserTitle: You noticed you were fine, and it startled you
moods.teaser: Something happened this week that you'd have expected to flatten you, and it didn't. You went about the day. You only noticed afterwards. That seems to be how it goes. Not a morning when you wake up healed — just a slow redistribution of weight, until the thing you're carrying has quietly changed shape.
moods.teaserTail: Part of you is suspicious of this. Waiting for it to be taken back.
moods.shareLine: Recovery isn't a line you cross. It's ordinary days, with fewer ambushes.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read when you're starting to feel better
moods.seoKeywords: something to read while healing, short writing about recovery, words for feeling better slowly
body: Something happened this week that you'd have expected to flatten you, and it didn't. You went about the day. You only noticed afterwards.
That seems to be how it goes. Not a morning when you wake up healed — just a slow redistribution of weight, until the thing you're carrying has quietly changed shape.
Part of you is suspicious of this. Waiting for it to be taken back. Treating a good week as weather rather than climate.
Let it be weather for now. You don't have to trust it in order to be in it.
You're allowed not to know whether you're over it. Recovery isn't a line you cross with a certificate. It's more and more ordinary days, with fewer and fewer ambushes.
Some of the old thing will stay. In time it becomes something you know, rather than something that happens to you.
You are further along than you were. That counts, even unfinished.

moods.name: Dread
moods.tagline: For the strange heaviness before Monday begins.
moods.description: A piece for the Sunday evening that starts leaving before it's over.
moods.whatThisIs: For the five o'clock feeling that isn't about anything in particular, and can't be fixed by making the most of it.
moods.teaserTitle: The evening starts leaving before it's over
moods.teaser: It arrives around five. Nothing has happened. The day was fine, maybe even good, and then something in the light changes and the weekend starts packing up without you. You're not dreading anything in particular. That's what makes it hard to argue with — there's no single thing you could fix tomorrow to make this evening feel different.
moods.teaserTail: What you're feeling is the edge of a week you haven't started yet, pressed against the last few hours of one that's nearly done.
moods.shareLine: Let it be an ordinary evening that happens to come before a Monday.
moods.seoTitle: Something to read on a Sunday night
moods.seoKeywords: something to read on sunday night, short writing about sunday scaries, words for dreading monday
body: It arrives around five. Nothing has happened. The day was fine, maybe even good, and then something in the light changes and the weekend starts packing up without you.
You're not dreading anything in particular. That's what makes it hard to argue with — there's no single thing you could fix tomorrow to make this evening feel different.
What you're feeling is the edge of a week you haven't started yet, pressed against the last few hours of one that's nearly done.
Everyone you know feels some version of this and almost nobody mentions it, which is why it can seem like a personal failing instead of a Sunday.
You don't have to make the most of the evening. That instruction is part of the problem — it turns the last few hours into one more thing to perform.
Let it be an ordinary evening that happens to come before a Monday.
The week will start whether you brace for it or not. You may as well not brace.
